decisions.reason: As a close extension of the firm's integrated airport operations software offer, it fits existing knowledge and customer relationships well, so strong absorptive capacity supports continued refinement rather than withdrawal.
This module builds directly on the firm's established apron and integration capabilities, making it easy to learn from early deployments and improve within the existing product system.

Although billing is somewhat less central than operational control, it still leverages the firm's airport data and software base, so management would likely retain it while testing how well it complements the wider platform.
Monitoring apron equipment is closely related to the firm's installed-base experience, maintenance know-how, and data-driven direction, which lowers the chance of an early exit.
Resource management is near the core of airport efficiency and turnaround optimization, so the firm can apply existing operational knowledge and service feedback to strengthen the product.

A controller safety alert service matches the firm's safety-critical airport systems expertise and benefits from in-house R&D, so management would be inclined to keep developing it despite potentially longer adoption cycles.
